_comment: GENERIC NAMES that are NOT a same-operator signal. WebPivot treats a shared distinctive subdomain label (svc-a.site-a.example) or a shared distinctive resource basename (index-B3GD2NjP.js) as an operator link. Every name listed here is used by millions of unrelated sites, so sharing one proves nothing and must never create a cluster. ADD a label when you see it produce a false link; REMOVE one only if you are confident it is rare enough to be distinctive — removing is the risky direction (it manufactures clusters).

subdomain_labels._comment: Leftmost subdomain LABELS that name infrastructure or a service rather than the operator. Matched EXACTLY against the leftmost label only. Consumed by wp_pivots._distinctive_subdomain: a host whose first label is in here yields no subdomain pivot.

resource_basename_segments._comment: Dot-separated SEGMENTS of a JS/CSS filename that name a library, build artifact or entry point rather than the operator's own build (jquery.min.js, app.js, gtm.js). Consumed by wp_analyze._is_distinctive_basename, which ignores these segments when deciding whether a basename carries a distinctive build hash worth a urlscan `filename:` reverse.
